title: The 7 Continents of the World
answer: There are 7 continents on Earth: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, and Australia (Oceania).
highlights: Largest by Area & Population: Asia (~4.7 billion people, 44.58 million km²)
Second Largest: Africa (~1.4 billion people, 30.37 million km²)
Third Largest: North America (~590 million people, 24.71 million km²)
Fourth Largest: South America (~430 million people, 17.84 million km²)
Coldest & Most Desolate: Antarctica (14.2 million km², no permanent human population)
Sixth Largest: Europe (~750 million people, 10.18 million km²)
Smallest by Land Area: Australia / Oceania (~43 million people, 8.6 million km²)

title: The 5 Oceans of the World
answer: There are 5 recognized oceans on Earth: Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern (Antarctic) Ocean, and Arctic Ocean.
highlights: Largest & Deepest: Pacific Ocean (Covers >30% of Earth surface, contains Mariana Trench)
Second Largest: Atlantic Ocean (Separates the Americas from Europe and Africa)
Third Largest: Indian Ocean (Warmest ocean, washes around Indian subcontinent)
Fourth Largest: Southern Ocean (Encircles Antarctica south of 60°S latitude)
Smallest & Shallowest: Arctic Ocean (Surrounds the North Pole, mostly covered by sea ice)

title: Mount Everest (Sagarmatha / Chomolungma) — Tallest Mountain
answer: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level, with an official elevation of 8,848.86 metres (29,031.7 ft). It is located in the Mahalangur Himal sub-range of the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and China (Tibet).
highlights: Location: Himalayas (Border of Nepal and Tibet Autonomous Region, China)
First Confirmed Ascent: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay (29 May 1953)

title: Nile River — Longest River in the World
answer: The Nile River is the longest river in the world, with an estimated length of 6,650 kilometres (4,132 miles), flowing northward through eleven countries in northeastern Africa into the Mediterranean Sea.
highlights: Primary Tributaries: White Nile and Blue Nile (meeting at Khartoum, Sudan)
Basin Countries: Egypt, Sudan, South Sudan, Ethiopia, Uganda, DR Congo, Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Eritrea
Significance: Provided life and fertile silt for Ancient Egyptian civilization

title: Amazon River — Largest River by Discharge Volume
answer: The Amazon River in South America is the largest river in the world by water discharge volume (accounting for roughly 20% of global river discharge into oceans) and the second longest at approximately 6,400 km (3,977 mi).
highlights: Discharge: ~209,000 m³/s (greater than the next seven largest rivers combined)
Drainage Basin: Amazon Basin (~7 million km² across Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Bolivia, Ecuador)
Biodiversity: Flows through the Amazon Rainforest, the world's most biodiverse tropical rainforest

title: Sahara Desert — Largest Hot Desert in the World
answer: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world and the third-largest desert overall (after Antarctica and the Arctic), covering an area of 9.2 million square kilometres (3.6 million sq mi) across Northern Africa.
highlights: Total Area: ~9,200,000 km² (comparable to the area of China or the United States)
Location: North Africa (spans 11 countries: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Sudan, Tunisia, Western Sahara)
Climate: Hyper-arid, with sand dunes (ergs) reaching up to 180 metres in height

title: Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) — Deepest Oceanic Trench
answer: The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean. Its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, reaches a depth of approximately 10,994 metres (36,070 ft / ~11 km) below sea level.
highlights: Maximum Depth: ~10,994 m (36,070 ft / nearly 11 km) at Challenger Deep
Location: Western Pacific Ocean, east of the Mariana Islands
Water Pressure: Exceeds 1,000 atmospheres (108.6 MPa) at the trench floor

title: Grand Canyon — Steep-Sided Canyon in Arizona, USA
answer: The Grand Canyon is a steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, United States. It is 446 km (277 mi) long, up to 29 km (18 mi) wide, and attains a depth of over 1,857 metres (6,093 feet).
highlights: Length & Depth: 446 km (277 miles) long, ~1,857 m (6,000 ft) deep
River: Carved over millions of years by the Colorado River
Status: UNESCO World Heritage Site and US National Park
